# {{projectName}} Architecture Patterns

Reference for the code ModMon scaffolds and the conventions that keep
modules isolated and extractable. Examples use a module named `Orders`.

## Module isolation

Each module is a vertical slice with its own DbContext, entities,
services, controllers, and migrations:

```
{{projectName}}.Orders/
├── AutoMapperProfiles/
├── Controllers/
├── Database/
│   ├── OrdersDbContext.cs          # sealed DbContext
│   ├── OrdersDbContextFactory.cs   # design-time factory for dotnet ef
│   ├── Entities/
│   ├── Migrations/                 # EF Core migrations (InitialCreate+)
│   └── Scripts/
│       ├── DbUpMigrator.cs         # TryMigrate entry point
│       ├── Versioned/001_init.sql  # runs once, in order
│       └── Repeatable/R__*.sql     # re-runnable objects (views etc.)
├── Exceptions/
├── Extensions/DependencyInjection.cs  # AddOrdersDI(...)
├── Interfaces/
├── Models/
└── Services/
```

The module csproj embeds `Database\Scripts\**\*.sql` so DbUp loads them
from the assembly. Module detection: a `{Project}.{X}` directory with a
matching `.csproj`, excluding `.Api`, `.SharedKernel`, and `*.Tests`.

## DI aggregation

Modules self-register via an extension method; the API aggregates them
between markers that `modmon module add` edits:

```csharp
// {{projectName}}.Orders/Extensions/DependencyInjection.cs
public static class DependencyInjection
{
    public static IServiceCollection AddOrdersDI(
        this IServiceCollection services,
        IConfiguration configuration)
    {
        var connectionString = configuration
            .GetConnectionString("DefaultConnection")
            ?? string.Empty;

        services.AddDbContext<OrdersDbContext>(options =>
            options.UseNpgsql(connectionString));

        // services.AddScoped<IOrderService, OrderService>();
        return services;
    }
}
```

```csharp
// {{projectName}}.Api/Extensions/DependencyInjection.cs
public static class DependencyInjection
{
    public static IServiceCollection AddProjectModules(
        this IServiceCollection services,
        IConfiguration configuration)
    {
        services.AddSharedKernelDI(configuration);
        // <modules>
        services.AddOrdersDI(configuration);
        // </modules>
        return services;
    }

    public static WebApplication ApplyProjectMigrations(
        this WebApplication app,
        IConfiguration configuration)
    {
        // <ef>
        MigrateDbContext<OrdersDbContext>(app);
        // </ef>
        // <dbup>
        ThrowIfFailed("Orders", OrdersDbUp.TryMigrate(configuration));
        // </dbup>
        return app;
    }
}
```

`MigrateDbContext<T>` opens a scope and calls `Database.Migrate()`;
`ThrowIfFailed` throws when `TryMigrate` returns non-zero. `Program.cs`
calls `builder.Services.AddProjectModules(configuration)` before
`builder.Build()` and `app.ApplyProjectMigrations(configuration)` after.

## Dual database migrations

Two systems run at startup, EF first — keep ownership disjoint.

### EF Core migrations — entity schema

- `module add` runs `dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate
  --output-dir Database/Migrations`. It needs the `dotnet-ef` tool; if
  absent, the module is still added with a warning — rerun manually.
- Applied at startup by `MigrateDbContext<T>` → `Database.Migrate()`.
- Add more with `dotnet ef migrations add <Name>
  --project {{projectName}}.Orders
  --startup-project {{projectName}}.Api`; the design-time
  `OrdersDbContextFactory` supplies the connection string.

### DbUp — supplemental objects

- `Versioned/*.sql` run once, in order. `Repeatable/*.sql` (views,
  functions, seed data) re-run when their content changes.
- `DbUpMigrator.TryMigrate` creates the `orders` schema if missing, then
  journals to `orders.schema_versions` and executes the embedded
  scripts.
- Scripts are selected by embedded-resource name
  (`.Database.Scripts.Versioned.` / `.Database.Scripts.Repeatable.`), so
  subfolders under `Scripts/` work.

### Ownership rule

EF migrations create the tables, columns, and indexes declared in the
DbContext model. DbUp creates everything EF does not model. If both
create the same object, the second runner fails at startup.

## SharedKernel — the only shared reference

`{{projectName}}.SharedKernel` ships:

| Area | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `Database/Entities` | `BaseEntity` (Id, audit user ids, UTC-coerced Created/ModifiedDate) |
| `Common` | `Constants.HttpContextKeys.REQUEST_ID_KEY` (`"RequestId"`) |
| `Exceptions` | `GenericExceptionModel`, `BaseBadRequestException` (→400), `BaseNotFoundException` (→404), `BaseConflictException` (→409) |
| `Extensions` | `DateTimeExtensions.ToUtc`, `AddSharedKernelDI` |
| `Middleware` | `RequestGuidMiddleware` (`X-RequestId` + log context), `GlobalExceptionHandlingMiddleware`, `ModelStateValidationFilter`, `DateTimeModelBinder(Provider)` |
| `Events` | `IEvent`, `IEventHandler<T>`, `IEventDispatcher`, `EventDispatcher` |

Put cross-module contracts, DTOs, and events here — never inside a
module project.

## Cross-module communication

### Synchronous — SharedKernel interface

1. Define `IProductService` + DTOs in `SharedKernel/Interfaces`.
2. Implement `ProductService` in the Products module and register it in
   `AddProductsDI`:
   `services.AddScoped<IProductService, ProductService>()`.
3. Inject `IProductService` into Orders services — Orders references
   SharedKernel only, never `{{projectName}}.Products`.

### Asynchronous — in-process events

1. Define the event as an `IEvent` in `SharedKernel/Events`. Events are
   contracts — defining one inside a module forces consumers to depend
   on that module.
2. Publish via `IEventDispatcher.DispatchAsync` (registered by
   `AddSharedKernelDI`; it fans out to every `IEventHandler<TEvent>`).
3. Handle in any module by registering
   `services.AddScoped<IEventHandler<OrderCreatedEvent>,
   OrderCreatedEventHandler>()` in that module's `Add{Module}DI`.

**Never:** inject another module's DbContext, add a module→module or
module→API project reference, or define shared events inside a module.

## Cross-cutting concerns (auto-wired in Program.cs)

- Serilog via `builder.Host.SerilogConfiguration()` — compact JSON to
  console (`RenderedCompactJsonFormatter`), `Microsoft` at Warning.
- `UseCors("AllowAll")`, Swagger in Development only,
  `RequestGuidMiddleware`, `GlobalExceptionHandlingMiddleware` (maps the
  `Base*` exceptions to 400/404/409/500 `GenericExceptionModel` bodies),
  auth, `UseSerilogRequestLogging`.
- Controllers get `DateTimeModelBinderProvider` (UTC coercion) and
  `ModelStateValidationFilter` (400 on invalid ModelState).

## Docker

Multi-stage `Dockerfile`: `dotnet/sdk:10.0` build →
`dotnet/aspnet:10.0-noble-chiseled` runtime on port 8080. `module add`
inserts `COPY ["{P}.{M}/{P}.{M}.csproj", "{P}.{M}/"]` between the
`# <modules>` markers — keep them. `docker compose up --build` runs the
API on :8080 plus a healthcheck-gated `postgres:16` on :5432 using the
named volume `{{projectNameLower}}_pgdata`.
